content: The Sweet Chestnut, scientifically known as Castanea sativa and belonging to the family Fagaceae, is also referred to as the Spanish Chestnut or European Chestnut. This species is native to southeastern Europe and Asia Minor. It is a deciduous tree that can grow to a height of 20 to 35 meters, with a trunk diameter often reaching 2 meters. The leaves are oblong-lanceolate in shape, boldly toothed, and measure between 16 to 28 cm in length and 5 to 9 cm in width. The tree produces flowers of both sexes on upright catkins that are 10 to 20 cm long. Male flowers are located in the upper part of the catkin, while female flowers are found in the lower part. These flowers typically appear between late June and July. By autumn, the female flowers develop into spiny cupules that contain 3 to 7 brownish nuts, which are shed in October. The bark of the tree often exhibits a net-shaped (retiform) pattern with deep furrows or fissures that spiral in both directions along the trunk. The Sweet Chestnut thrives in mild climates with adequate moisture, which are essential for optimal growth and nut production. However, it is sensitive to late spring and early autumn frosts and does not tolerate lime-rich soils. Under forest conditions, the tree can adapt to moderate shade. The Sweet Chestnut has been widely cultivated for its edible nuts. Its cultivation dates back to Roman times when it was introduced to more northern regions. Later, monks cultivated it in monastery gardens. Today, centuries-old specimens can be found in Great Britain and throughout central and western Europe. The nuts are commonly used by confectioners and are also consumed roasted. They are particularly popular in countries such as Turkey, Portugal, France, Italy, and Corsica. The nuts can be roasted whole or ground into flour. In Corsica, a variety of polenta, known as pulenta, is made using sweet chestnut flour. Additionally, a local Corsican beer incorporates chestnuts as an ingredient. The fruit of the Japanese chestnut is also edible. The wood of the Sweet Chestnut is durable and is used in the production of furniture, barrels (sometimes for aging balsamic vinegar), fencing, and roof beams in houses in the Alpujarra region of Spain. However, due to its tendency to split and warp, it is not suitable for use in large pieces. The bark of the tree is also a source of tannin.
